name: The St. Regis Saadiyat Island Resort
positioning: Beachfront St. Regis resort on Saadiyat Island in Abu Dhabi, overlooking the Arabian Gulf and the Saadiyat Beach Golf Club, a few minutes from the Louvre Abu Dhabi
best_for: Golfers who want to stay beside a beachfront course designed by Gary Player
Travelers pairing beach days with a visit to the Louvre Abu Dhabi

facts.text: The resort overlooks a beach, the Arabian Gulf and the Saadiyat Beach Golf Club.
The resort is a few minutes from the Louvre Abu Dhabi.
The Saadiyat Beach Golf Club course was designed by Gary Player.
Every room and suite has a private balcony and St. Regis Butler service available day or night.
The resort pairs Mediterranean-inspired architecture with contemporary interiors and natural materials.
The Royal Suite is a duplex across the hotel's top two levels.
Oléa is a Mediterranean-inspired all-day restaurant with indoor and outdoor seating and live cooking stations.
Afternoon tea at Café Ginori Saadiyat Island is served on Ginori 1735 porcelain.
The resort has two outdoor, lighted hard tennis courts with complimentary rackets and balls.
The head concierge is a member of Les Clefs d'Or.
The resort is on Condé Nast Traveler's Gold List 2026.

highlights.text: The Saadiyat Beach Golf Club was the Arabian Gulf's first beachfront golf course.
Hawksbill turtles find refuge in the beach dunes and dolphins play in the surf along the shore.
Sontaya serves Southeast Asian food and sits among a series of interconnected pools overlooking the beach.
The Manhattan Lounge serves the Arabian Snapper, the hotel's Bloody Mary made with zaatar.
The resort opened in December 2011 as the St. Regis brand's first property in the Middle East.

considerations.text: Guest rooms and suites are being enhanced in phases until the end of 2027.
WhataHotel notes the island location requires travel time to reach the Abu Dhabi city center.
WhataHotel notes premium luxury pricing reflecting the high-end positioning.
